minutes_text:
March 22, 2018
  6:00 P.M.
  Council Chambers of City Hall
  340 Palos Verdes Dr. West
  Palos Verdes Estates

  Meeting Summary
  OF THE
  FINANCE ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  OF THE CITY OF PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

CALL TO ORDER

6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

All members present

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Motion by Vice Chair Young. Second by Committee Member McGowan. Unanimously approved.

NEW BUSINESS

1. Welcome and Introductions

  Mayor Vandever welcomed the Committee and described the role and purpose of the
  Committee. Each Committee Member provided a self-introduction. Each City staff person
  present introduced him/herself.

2. Swearing-in of Committee Members and Review of Guiding Principles

  City Clerk Pettit administered the Oath of Office to the Committee members. City Attorney
  Hogin explained the laws pertaining to conflict of interest and Ms. Pettit explained Form 700
  that each Committee member must complete. Ms. Hogin explained the Ralph M. Brown Act

   and the requirements pertaining to public records.  General guidelines were presented for
  conducting meetings.

3. Discussion of Committee Goals and Objectives

  City Manager Dahlerbruch presented Ordinance 17-727 describing the purpose and focus of the
  Committee. Committee Members identified goals and objectives for the Committee as follows:

  Objectives

  •  Be a window to the public on information about the City’s budget and finances
  o Develop a platform to communicate to the public
  o Explain information to the public
  o Create a “dashboard” view
  •  Review structural balance of the budget for/during the annual budget approval process
  •  Provide format and frequency of budget review
  o Including comparison of budget to actual so readers can see the status of the budget at
  any time
  o Conduct quarterly reviews of the budget status
  o Create “dashboard” of performance indicators
  •  Meeting before the City Council meets to review “dashboards” and quarterly reports
  •  Look at base operational budget to project revenues and expenses to determine if there is a
  structural balance
  •  Use GFOA (Government Finance Officers Association) worksheets to calculate and
  determine appropriate reserve levels
  o Upon completing analysis, prepare a 5 and 10 year projection
  •  Create a glossary of terms for the budget so there is consistency of terms and clarity in what
  they mean
  •  Address long-term infrastructure and capital items
  o Create a plan that is separate from the operations
  o Separate maintenance costs from capital projects
  o Prioritize the capital projects
  •  Improve communications and develop a communications strategy
  •  Look at revenue situation and options for future revenue
  •  Look at pension costs
  o Both CalPERS and LACERA
  •  Evaluate the revenue stream in relation to expenditures
  •  Meet more frequently
  •  Create a Financial Policy
  •  Create performance measures to evaluate outcomes – to assess if goals are being achieved
  •  For each Ad Hoc Committee to develop a mission statement

   Goals

  •  Ad Hoc Committee on “Capital” and Ad Hoc Committee on “Operating” (budget,
  performance and forecasting) for preparing a “big picture” projection

  •  Create a plan that balances revenues and expenditures

  •  Communicate to the City Council and public

  •  Identify/propose fixes to problem areas

  The Committee identified and determined to establish the following five Ad Hoc Committees.

  1. Communications and Messaging for developing information in a way that is easy
  for the public to understand (Amy Forte and Don Culler)

  2. Operating Budget for determining if the budget is structurally balanced (by
  developing and analyzing projections), determining the status and appropriate amount
  for a fiscal reserve, assessing the status of the budget, creating a model to present
  year-to-date performance, reviewing CJPIA costs, etc. (Mark Young and David
  McGowan)

  3. Capital Improvement, Maintenance and Equipment Replacement to assess and
  develop long range projections and determine if funds from the Capital Improvement
  Program budget and Equipment Replacement used to balance the FY 2017-18 budget
  should be backfilled (Don Culler and Ela Jhaveri)

  4. Pension and Benefits to evaluate, assess, and plan for employee costs, and to assess
  County pension impacts related to the City’s contract for Fire and Paramedic services
  (Victoria Lozzi and Ela Jhaveri)

  5. Revenue Opportunities to determine how and where new revenue sources can be
  established (Victoria Lozzi)

  The Ad Hoc Committees were directed to develop its mission and goals and report back
  to the full Committee at its next meeting.

  The Committee directed that future agendas include Ad Hoc Committee reports for
  updates on each Ad Hoc Committee’s work and progress.

4. Overview Presentation of City organization, Budget, Expenses and Projected Long-Range
  Fiscal Challenges

  The City’s external auditor with White Nelson Diehl Evans LLP, Daphne Munoz, provided an
  overview of the City’s 2016-17 Comprehensive Annual Financial Report. The City Treasurer
  provided an overview of the City’s investment policy and investments. An overview of the

   operating budget and mid-year report, capital program and long-range fiscal issues affecting
  cities was continued to the next Committee meeting.

5. Review of Calendar and Agendas for Next Quarterly Meetings

  The Committee voted to meet on April 19, May 17 and June 21; however, June 21 may change
  in addition to participating in the City Council’s budget workshop. The Committee requested
  that the City Council be advised and requested to approve the monthly meetings.

WRITTEN COMMUNICATION (Attachment A)

  No action.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

Speakers:
  Rose Ramsey
  Ed Kennedy
  Council Member Sanford Davidson

ADJOURNMENT

9:00 p.m.
